articles.title: NFL Trade Deadline Grades: Who Won The DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson Deals?
articles.summary: Who has won the most notable trades ahead of the deadline? We grade all the top deals.
articles.body: And just like that, the NFL trade deadline season has arrived. The Indianapolis Colts made sure of that on Tuesday. They traded a pair of franchise cornerstones within a few hours, agreeing to deals to trade defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers and guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. We'll almost certainly see more trades to come over the next couple of weeks, and all signs indicate that Indianapolis might not be done trading yet. But as we await more trades, let's grade the deals the Colts made on Tuesday as we inch closer to the Nov. 10 trade deadline. 49ers Get DeForest Buckner Back 49ers receive: DT DeForest Buckner Colts receive: 2027 fourth-round pick Eric D. Williams: The Indianapolis Colts shipped Buckner back to the team that selected him as the seventh overall pick of the 2016 draft as part of that team’s fire sale. Indianapolis received a fourth-round pick for the 32-year-old rangy defensive tackle. A cornerstone for the Colts defensively, Buckner has four sacks, eight quarterback hits and 31 combined tackles in seven games. Buckner should give San Francisco a pass rush boost. The 49ers finished with a league-low 20 sacks last season and this year hasn’t been much better, with 15 sacks (tied for 20th) so far this season. The 49ers are expecting the team’s best pass rusher, Nick Bosa, to return at some point this season from a calf injury. Paired with his former teammate in Buckner, the two should form a potent pass-rushing tandem for San Francisco, which is expected to compete for a deep postseason run. For the Colts, they get some draft compensation to start the rebuilding process after a disappointing start to the season that led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. But they’re also giving up a foundational player who is still productive and a leader within their organization and still has good ball left in him. The draft compensation is on the low side for a player of Buckner’s stature, even though he’s on an expiring contract and set to hit free agency at the end of this year. 49ers grade: B+ Colts grade: C+ Seahawks Land Quenton Nelson Seahawks receive: G Quenton Nelson Colts receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick Ben Arthur: This was a brilliant move by Seahawks general manager John Schneider. In Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler and six-time All-Pro selection, Seattle gets a massive boost for Sam Darnold’s protection and an anchor upfront for what’s been an uneven rushing attack through seven weeks. With the Seahawks set to receive a third-round pick for losing executive Nolan Teasley, who became the Minnesota Vikings’ general manager, the team still has a third-round selection for 2027. And Seattle is also set to receive two fifth-round compensatory picks this year (free-agent departures of Kenneth Walker III, Riq Woolen), so a 2028 fifth-rounder is even more palpable than it already was for a player of Nelson’s caliber. The Nelson deal kicked off the Colts’ fire sale and was necessary, as Indianapolis needs all the picks it can get to supercharge a rebuild without a first-round pick. articles.title: Rays Stay Alive: 4 Takeaways From Tampa Bay's World Series Game 4 Win vs. Brewers
articles.summary: With their season on life support, the Rays put on pressure in the bottom of the 12th, delivering the Brewers a taste of their own medicine.
articles.body: The ball traveled 396 feet off the bat of Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt and into the left-field bleachers in the 12th inning at Tropicana Park, seeming less like a floating orb and more like a darting dagger delivered directly to the hearts of Rays’ fans. But Tampa Bay wasn’t ready for its season to end. These Rays can fight back, too. With their season on life support after Pratt’s go-ahead blast, they put on pressure in the bottom of the 12th, delivering the Brewers a taste of their own medicine. And after a fielding error and four straight singles, the Rays ensured their season would live on at least another day. Only four of the previous 25 teams to go down 3-0 in a best-of-seven World Series had even forced a Game 5. As Tuesday night gave way to Wednesday morning, the Rays became the fifth. Here are my takeaways from Tampa Bay’s 4-3 Game 4 win. 1. Rays Didn't Roll Over If anyone thought a 10-1 loss in Game 3 and a 3-0 series deficit would make the Rays roll over in Game 4, Tampa Bay made clear from the start that wouldn’t be the case. An RBI single from Chandler Simpson gave the Rays an early lead. As they have done all year, the Brewers answered back to tie the game in the fourth. But this time, the Rays were ready to respond, answering back quickly and forcing mistakes. Junior Caminero singled, moved to second on a groundout by Liam Hicks, then scored on an error. On a grounder by Jonny DeLuca, Caminero avoided a tag by Brewers third baseman David Hamilton, who then tried to get the speedy DeLuca at first base. The off-balance throw across the diamond was way off target, getting past first baseman Jake Bauers and allowing Caminero to score the go-ahead run. The Brewers challenged to see if Hamilton made the tag — Caminero drifted into the infield grass to try to avoid the tag but was not ruled out of the baseline, which is not reviewable — and that was unsuccessful. Surprisingly, the typically surehanded Brewers committed more than twice as many errors as any other team this postseason. But they often found ways to redeem themselves. Tuesday was no different. But the Rays countered every punch, none more important than the 12th. Another error by a Brewers third baseman, this one by Joey Ortiz, allowed Caminero to reach base to start the inning. Brewers manager Pat Murphy turned to Shane Drohan. Hicks singled, DeLuca hit a game-tying single, Chandler Simpson loaded the bases with a single and Ben Williamson chopped a grounder over the infield, emptying the home dugout as his teammates mobbed in shallow right field, right where his chopper landed. 2. The Rookie Was Ready It surprised many when the Brewers gave Pratt an eight-year contract extension in April. At the time, the then-21-year-old had yet to make his MLB debut and had only a handful of Triple-A at-bats under his belt. "I think Brewers fans will fall in love with him," Brewers manager Pat Murphy claimed at the time. Six months later, Pratt nearly won them the World Series. The Milwaukee shortstop started the scoring for the Brewers with a game-tying RBI double in the fourth as "COOOOP" chants from the loud Brewers contingent in the crowd echoed through Tropicana Field. They would get louder eight innings later, when he launched a 396-foot, game-winning solo home run off Ian Seymour in the 12th. The rookie finished the night 4-for-5 and knocked in runs in each of the last three games of the series, clearly unintimidated by baseball’s biggest stage. 3. David Hamilton Got His Redemption As it usually goes for these Brewers players, Hamilton quickly found a way to make up for his blunder. In the clinching Game 4 of the National League Championship Series, it was third baseman Hamilton who was the unlikely home run hero when he came through with a solo shot off Dodgers closer Edwin Díaz to give the Brewers some breathing room and help cement their first trip to the World Series since 1982. Hamilton only had four home runs on the year to that point, including just one in the season’s second half. Yet in another Game 4 clinching scenario, this time in the World Series, he was back at it again. Immediately after his fourth-inning error put the Rays ahead, Hamilton serendipitously found himself up to bat first the following inning. Griffin Jax had given the Rays everything they could have asked for to that point, holding the unrelenting Brewers offense to just a run through four innings, when manager Kevin Cash hoped he could get one more against the Brewers’ No. 9 hitter. Hamilton had different thoughts, launching an 0-2 four-seamer at the top of the zone 391-feet for a game-tying home run. That was Jax’s final batter of the game, and the latest example of a Brewers team that never goes away. It was also a similar scenario to Game 2 of the World Series, when an error from rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt started the Rays’ four-run first inning. In the seventh inning of that game, Pratt atoned for his mistake by finishing off the Brewers’ comeback with the game-winning RBI single. Of course, Pratt’s best was yet to come. 4. Brewers’ Bullpen Rest Paid Off … Until The End After pulling out tight wins all October, the Brewers finally got to breathe a little bit in a 10-1 win in Game 3. That commanding victory almost meant they didn’t have to use any of their high-leverage relievers, who were well-rested as they waited in the wings Tuesday night. That spelled trouble for Tampa Bay in Game 4. The Brewers’ bullpen entered the night 8-1 with a 1.34 ERA and eight saves during the postseason. Those numbers got even better Tuesday night. Murphy turned the game to his bullpen in the fourth inning, starting with a scoreless fourth from JoJo Romero. Abner Uribe, pitching for the 10th time this October, followed with two scoreless frames. Then came DL Hall with 1 ⅔ scoreless innings and Trevor Megill with an inning-ending strikeout, setting the stage for the incomparable Aaron Ashby. The shutdown lefty retired all seven batters he faced, running his playoff record to 18 consecutive relief innings this October. But he could only go so long. The Brewers’ bullpen went eight scoreless innings until the train came off the tracks when the high-leverage weapons were gone in the 12th. 4 ½. What's Next? Jacob Misiorowski, the NL Cy Young favorite, is coming off his most productive outing of the postseason, though he has yet to showcase the form that made him the most unhittable starter in MLB. The Brewers saved him for Game 5, rather than burning him in at some point in Tuesday night’s marathon, and he’ll now have a chance to deliver the Brewers their first World Series title. On the other side, the Rays had yet to reveal their Game 5 plan in the immediate aftermath of the win. After Game 1 starter Nick Martinez pitched two innings of relief in Game 4, it’s possible that they turn to Drew Rasmussen for Game 5 on three days of rest in an effort to send the series back to Milwaukee. If they’re able to do that, they’ll make history in the process. Of the four other teams to make it to a Game 5 after going down 3-0 in the World Series, none have forced a Game 6.

articles.title: Derek Jeter Warns Brewers That World Series Game 4 Loss Can't 'Deflate' Them
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers will have to wait for their championship celebration, but Derek Jeter says they still have little reason to feel deflated.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers will have to wait for their World Series championship celebration. The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Brewers 4-3 in 12 innings on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field on Ben Williamson’s walk-off single, avoiding elimination and forcing a Game 5 on Wednesday. Brewers manager Pat Murphy’s message to the Brewers after their heartbreaking Game 4 loss was simple: Tampa Bay will go into Game 5 feeling good, and they should too. Derek Jeter thinks Murphy is spot-on. "He said it was going to be hard. He understands this," the five-time World Series champion said. "It's as good as Tampa feels right now coming into tomorrow, because they’re going to sleep well. "If you’re the Brewers, you can’t allow this to deflate you, because if someone told you in spring training you’d be up three games to one in the World Series with your ace on the mound, the best pitcher in all of baseball on the mound, they would all take it." Murphy credited Tampa Bay and said Milwaukee has to move on quickly. "It’s going to be hard. You’re playing the best team in the American League," Murphy said. "They proved it all year long, and they came up big today. When you’re achieving something like this, it’s going to have its adversity." Murphy confirmed Jacob Misiorowski would start on the mound for Game 5, and he added that it will be "all hands on deck." Milwaukee leads the World Series 3-1 and Jeter said both teams should be confident heading into Game 5. "You’ve got two clubhouses that are feeling pretty good coming in tomorrow night," he said. articles.title: Players Championship 31: Charlie Manby wins first ever PDC Ranking title and confirm Grand Slam qualification
articles.summary: Charlie Manby confirmed his spot in the Grand Slam of Darts with his victory at Players Championship 31; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Manby celebrated a milestone victory in the Netherlands, producing a series of dominant displays to also confirm his qualification for next month's Grand Slam of Darts.

The 21-year-old had not progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a PDC ranking event prior to Wednesday, but he reaffirmed his potential to pocket the £15,000 top prize on Dutch soil.

"It's absolutely amazing. I'm literally lost for words here," Manby said.

"There are so many good players here, so it's just crazy that I've actually done it.

"I knew I was definitely capable of doing what I did today and winning a title, but I'm over the moon.

"When I was leading against Beau [Greaves] in the semis, that's when I had a bit of nerves, especially when she started coming back!

"I was gutted to lose out in the World Youth Championship semi-finals for the Grand Slam, but I've managed to actually qualify through this which is 10 times better, so it's great."

Manby opened his campaign in style, averaging 104 in his 6-1 demolition of the Czech Republic's Karel Sedlacek, before landing back-to-back 13-darters to complete a comeback win over Dennie Olde Kalter.

The Huddersfield youngster then followed up a 6-4 success against Adam Leek with an inspired 112.16 average against Dominik Gruellich, winning each of his last four legs in 12 darts to race into the last eight.

Manby later reeled off six consecutive legs from 3-0 adrift to sink Alan Soutar, although he was forced to survive a fightback himself from Greaves to prevail 7-5 in a compelling semi-final.

This set up a winner-takes-all clash against Kuivenhoven, and Manby punished a tentative start from the Dutchman to race into a seemingly unassailable five-leg lead.

Greaves also performed magnificently at Maassport Den Bosch to climb up to seventh spot on the Players Championship rankings.

The Doncaster darter produced ton-topping averages in statement wins against Dutch duo Niels Zonneveld and Kevin Doets, launching an astonishing fightback from 5-2 down against the latter.

Earlier in the day, Spanish No 1 Cristo Reyes found a nine-darter during his opening-round drubbing of Cor Dekker - his second perfect leg in the space of three Players Championship events.

Elsewhere in Den Bosch, Nathan Aspinall was among the high-profile round one casualties, as Jermaine Wattimena, Damon Heta and Joe Cullen also bowed out at the first hurdle.

articles.title: WWE Icon Ric Flair Shares Health Update in Photo After Eye Injury Suffered During Fall
articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair gave another update on his health Wednesday after suffering a fall last week.
articles.body:
WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair gave another update on his health Wednesday after suffering a fall last week.

In a post on X, Flair shared a photo of himself posing with multiple doctors and noted that he will be "good to go" after "one more surgery and one more possible skin graft."

TMZ Sports reported that Flair fell outside a Florida restaurant last Friday, causing him to suffer eye and facial injuries. An ambulance transported Flair to a local hospital after the fall.

One day later, Flair divulged in a post on X that he had been released from the hospital and was going to be "okay."

Included in the post was a photo of Flair with a patch over one of his eyes.

The 77-year-old Flair is widely regarded as one of the greatest professional wrestlers of all time, having been a major world champion on 16 different occasions.

Flair has dealt with numerous health issues over the past several years, including undergoing emergency surgery to remove part of his bowel in 2017.

He recovered to the point that he was able to wrestle the final match of his illustrious career in 2022, teaming with Andrade El Idolo to beat Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal.

Most recently, Flair has worked with AEW, making periodic appearances for the company since 2023.

articles.title: Unrivaled Rosters to Be Revealed on B/R App, YouTube with Renee Montgomery and Chelsea Gray
articles.summary: Bleacher Report will host the 2027 Unrivaled roster reveal ahead of the league's third season.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report will host the 2027 Unrivaled roster reveal ahead of the league's third season.

The broadcast will air Nov. 4 at 7 p.m. ET on the B/R app and Bleacher Report's YouTube channe l. TNT Sports' Renee Montgomery will host the proceedings, with 2026 Unrivaled MVP Chelsea Gray providing her analysis.

The players will once again be split evenly between eight clubs: Breeze BC, Hive BC, Laces BC, Lunar Owls BC, Mist BC, Phantom BC, Rose BC and Vinyl BC.

Mist BC bested Phantom BC in the 2026 championship game. The New York Liberty's Breanna Stewart led all scorers with 32 points, while the Dallas Wings' Arike Ogunbowale came off the bench to score 19. A double-double from Washington Mystics forward Kiki Iriafen (13 points, 11 rebounds) wasn't enough for the Phantom.

Gray was crowned the MVP after leading Unrivaled in assists (6.1) and finishing second behind Marina Mabrey in scoring (24.2). The award was another accolade to add to a Hall of Fame career.

The 2027 campaign is scheduled to tip off Jan. 8 in Boston. The regular season will conclude with four games on March 5.

After the success of taking Unrivaled on the road to Philadelphia earlier this year, the league is expanding its list of outside markets. In addition to Boston for opening night, the league will stage games in Inglewood, California, Brooklyn, New York, San Francisco, Minneapolis and Houston.

Sephora Arena will remain Unrivaled's regular home for action.

articles.title: Ric Flair reveals injured eye after scary fall as WWE legend faces one more surgery and possible skin graft
articles.summary: WWE legend Ric Flair has shared a new update on his recovery after a fall in Tampa, Florida, left him with cuts to his head and eye and sent him to the
articles.body: WWE legend Ric Flair has shared a new update on his recovery after a fall in Tampa, Florida, left him with cuts to his head and eye and sent him to the hospital. The 77-year-old wrestler says he needs one more surgery and may also require a skin graft before he can fully recover. His latest photo with medical staff at USF Health offers fans a closer look at how he is doing.Ric Flair shows his injured eye after hospital stay in TampaRic Flair shared the recovery update on Wednesday, October 28, posting a photo with medical staff at USF Health in Florida. Along with the picture, he gave fans a clear idea of what remains before he can return to normal life. “One more surgery and one more possible skin graft, and then I will be good to go!” Flair wrote on X.His message suggests that he is making progress, although he still needs further medical care. The possible skin graft means doctors may need to use skin tissue to help repair the injured area. However, Flair has not shared further details about the planned procedure or confirmed when it will take place.The latest picture also gives fans a better view of his injured eye. In the days after the accident, Flair had been seen wearing an eye patch, which covered the affected area. His new post has now offered a clearer look at the injury as he continues to recover.Ric Flair’s fall outside Wagamama led to hospital treatmentThe accident happened on Friday, October 23, outside a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa, according to TMZ Sports, which first reported the incident. Flair suffered cuts to his head and eye, and an ambulance took him to the hospital. He reportedly remained there for more than 12 hours before being released.The fall raised concerns among fans, especially given Flair’s long career in professional wrestling and his past health struggles. However, he and his daughter, WWE superstar Charlotte Flair, later reassured people that he was doing okay. Flair also thanked those who had contacted him to check on his condition.After leaving the hospital, Flair shared a selfie the following morning, giving fans an early update on his condition. He also attended an event over the weekend, showing that he was able to make a public appearance despite the injury. However, the eye patch he wore meant people could not see the full extent of the damage.His latest photo and message provide a more detailed update, confirming that his recovery is not yet complete. While he remains hopeful about getting back to normal, the next surgery and the possibility of a skin graft are still ahead of him.For now, Flair has not announced a confirmed date for the procedure. articles.title: Manchester City 2 Brighton 2: City player ratings as the Carabao Cup holders march on
articles.summary: Manchester City 2 (Mateo Kovacic 40′, Vitor Reis 72′)Brighton 2 (Malick Yaicouyé 30′, Georginio Rutter 47′)Manchester City win 4-3 on penalties.Here are the...
articles.body:
Manchester City 2 (Mateo Kovacic 40′, Vitor Reis 72′)

Brighton 2 (Malick Yaicouyé 30′, Georginio Rutter 47′)

Here are the Manchester City player ratings as the club have progressed to the fifth round of the Carabao Cup after beating Brighton 4-3 on penalties at the Etihad Stadium tonight. The match finished 2-2 after 90 minutes. Both teams attacked throughout the game in what turned out to be a pulsating Carabao Cup tie.

Brighton took the lead twice as Malick Yaicouyé opened the scoring in the 31st minute. Mateo Kovacic equalised for Enzo Maresca's side in the 40th minute with a composed finish. Georginio Rutter restored Brighton's lead in the 47th minute before Vitor Reis cleverly turned in a Rayan Cherki free kick to make it 2-2 in the 72nd minute. Both teams pushed for a winner but the game ended 2-2 after 90 minutes.

A penalty shootout would decide the fourth round Carabao Cup tie. After Mateo Kovacic saw his spot kick saved by Brighton keeper Jason Steele, it seemed like Fabian Hurzeler's side had the advantage in the shootout. However, Gerónimo Rulli saved Yasin Ayari's spot kick before Rayan Cherki calmly gave Manchester a 4-2 lead. Rulli would then deny Brighton captain Lewis Dunk to seal Manchester City's progression to the fifth round of the Carabao Cup.

Manchester City's defence of the trophy they won last season marches on after an enthralling cup tie at the Etihad Stadium tonight. My City player ratings can be seen below.

Enzo Maresca took the opportunity to rotate his squad tonight. Maresca's selections

Gerónimo Rulli- 8.5/10: An extremely impressive display in goal from Rulli. He made one exceptional save and was City's hero in the penalty shootout.

Rico Lewis- 6/10: Lewis got on the ball often but his lack of defensive awareness did cost his team tonight. He must improve that side of his game.

Vitor Reis- 8/10: Reis was composed at the back throughout the match. Whether that was in possession or defensively. He grabbed his first City goal and he must start playing more often.

Marc Guehi- 6.5/10: A couple of nervy moments at the back from Guehi but he was better than previous games.

Nico O'Reilly- 6/10: He looks short of a gallop and will be better after getting minutes into his legs.

Ayyoub Bouaddi- 7.5/10: For the 45 minutes he was on the pitch he was superb. His composure in the face of Brighton's press was a sight to behold.

Mateo Kovacic- 7.5/10: The Croatian midfielder grabbed a goal and was good in midfield throughout the game I thought.

Phil Foden- 8/10: Some quality touched throughout the night from Foden and he was a constant attacking threat.

Rayan Cherki- 8.5/10: Cherki grabbed an assist and he was brilliant overall in an open match that suited him.

Allan- 6.5/10: I'd like to see him get on the ball more often but he does work tirelessly.

Floyd Samba- 6/10: He played a role in Kovacic's goal but was on the periphery of the match, however he showed touches of class at times.

Rayan Ait-Nouri- 7/10: Ait-Nouri offered plenty on both sides of the ball as he put in a performance he needed for his own confidence.

Ryan McAidoo- 6/10: He toiled away without influencing proceedings.

Jeremy Doku- 7.5/10: It did seem late on that Doku would be Manchester City's match-winner as he gave the Brighton defence fits.

Abdukodir Khusanov- 6/10: He came on late and was lively on both sides of the ball.

Enzo Fernandez- 6/10: Brought on late for the penalty shootout and did his job when he expertly converted his spot kick.

articles.title: Aaron Jones out of practice with a knee injury
articles.summary: Reports were that Vikings running back Aaron Jones avoided a serious injury last Sunday, but his practice work is still being managed this week.
articles.body:
Reports were that Vikings running back Aaron Jones avoided a serious injury last Sunday, but his practice work is still being managed this week.

The Vikings' first injury report of the week shows that Jones did not practice on Wednesday. Jones aggravated a knee injury in the second half of Minnesota's win over the Colts and word is that he is considered day-to-day heading into Sunday's game against the Lions.

Jordan Mason led the team in rushing against the Colts and would be in line for an even bigger role if Jones isn't able to play this week.

Guard Joe Huber (knee) was also out of practice for the Vikings. Right tackle Brian O'Neill (knee) was a limited participant.

articles.title: Celtic held to draw against Dundee United at Paradise
articles.summary: Scottish PremiershipWednesday, October 28, 2026Celtic ParkCELTIC…2(Durán 18, Scales 65)DUNDEE UNITED…2(Sapsford 28, Farrugia 31) It was a frustrating night f...
articles.body:
Scottish PremiershipWednesday, October 28, 2026Celtic Park

DUNDEE UNITED…2 (Sapsford 28, Farrugia 31)

It was a frustrating night for Celtic as the Bhoys were held to a 2-2 against Dundee United on Wednesday evening.

Martin O'Neill's side made a positive start to proceedings at Paradise, opening the scoring through Camilo Durán on 18 minutes.

However, the away side responded towards the end of the half, turning things round with two goals through Zac Sapsford and Neil Farrugia.

After finding themselves down at the break, Celtic produced a response, levelling up the scoring via Liam Scales just after the hour mark, but it ultimately wasn't enough to seal all three points.

As Martin O'Neill's side made their return to league action at Celtic Park, the manager named an unchanged side from the 2-1 win over Hibernian at the weekend.

And the Hoops were on the front foot early on, with Kasper Høgh having an opportunity in the opening stages. The Danish forward did well to attack Kieran Tierney's delivery into the box after wrestling with his marker but couldn't quite hit the target with his effort.

Celtic continued to attack as Liam Scales went close to opening the scoring with a header from a corner, but it went just passed the post, with the defender unfortunate not to find the bottom corner.

The Hoops finally got their reward for their positive start on 18 minutes as Camilo Durán opened the scoring, grabbing a goal for the fourth successive league fixture.

A ball into the box was headed back across goal by Benjamin Nygren, who looked to pick out a team-mate with his header.

He found the feet of Kasper Høgh, who laid it off for Durán to tuck home into the back of the net to give the Celts a well-deserved early advantage.

Celtic quickly looked to find a second, and came close through Nygren, who was unlucky not to find the target after another nice piece of set-up play by Høgh.

As the first-half wore on, the game took a turn as Dundee United fired home two quick-fire goals to turn things around in the opening 45 minutes.

The visitors' first goal came from a well-taken header by Zac Sapsford, who made the run across his marker, flicking an effort into the far bottom corner of the net.

And it took the away side just three minutes to find the net again, this time via Neil Farrugia, who fired United in front.

A corner into the box appeared to cause chaos in the box, which allowed the 27-year-old to divert the ball into the back of the net amidst a whole host of bodies inside the Celtic area.

With the Hoops finding themselves behind at the break, the manager made two changes, with Jota and Haissem Hassan replacing Callum Osmand and Kasper Høgh.

The two wide-men looked to cause danger for the Dundee United defence, consistently picking up the ball, and driving at either full-back.

Hassan in particular was unfortunate not to find his first goal in Celtic colours, with the winger stinging the gloves of the United shot-stopper, forcing a corner.

The Celts had plenty of set-plays to try and find their way back into the match in the second half, and that is where their leveller would come from.

After taking a short corner, the ball was worked to Jota, who floated a lovely looping cross into the box. That allowed time for Liam Scales to make a late run and attack the ball, his header finding the corner with his effort to make it 2-2.

As the Bhoys pushed for an all-important winner, they had to remain switched on as United themselves tried to find a third goal.

On a few occasions, the away side looked to hit on the attack at pace, with Sam Johnstone forced into a couple of smart stops.

Celtic piled on the pressure in the closing stages, as O'Neill also introduced Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka to the game.

A number of Celtic players tried their luck from distance on the edge of the box, with Oxlade-Chamberlain firing wide of the target.

The away side were also doing well to get bodies in front of the ball and blocked any effort on Jack Walton's goal.

Despite all the late pressure, it ultimately wasn't enough for the Hoops, who were forced to take away a share of the spoils at Celtic Park.

articles.title: Nathaniel Brown says Bayern Munich ‘deserved the win’ against FC Magdeburg
articles.summary: FC Bayern cruised past FC Magdeburg in the second round of the DFB-Pokal.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich easily dispatched a hopeful FC Magdeburg side in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday, scoring five assisted goals plus a penalty kick. Michael Olise recorded a brace while Ismael Saibari, Alphonso Davies, Nathaniel Brown, and David Santos Daiber also added to the scoring spree. Interim manager Aaron Danks used an experienced squad around 18-year old Lennart Karl, who featured impressively as the central attacking midfielder.

After the match (via @iMiaSanMia ), Brown was quick to praise his team's effort and turn the focus to Der Klassiker .

"We want to win every game, regardless of the opponent," said Brown. "We wanted to get through this Pokal tie. We had a good performance and deserved the win. Now we're focusing on Saturday. We're also winning for [Vincent Kompany], of course. It's really good that he's back home now. He should get some rest, but I hope we'll see him again soon."

Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane warmed up throughout the match but went unused as a reserve thanks to the favorable scoreline. Dayot Upamecano and Kim Min-jae were also allowed to rest in anticipation of the upcoming showdown with Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

articles.title: Browns Star Sits Out Practice as Injury Concerns Raised
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are playing a big game on Sunday against the Steelers. Will Jared Verse be healthy for it? The post Browns Star Sits Out Practice as Inj...
articles.body:
It's precautionary, but for the Cleveland Browns, having a player not practicing here just days before a critical showdown against the Steelers in the AFC North is cause for some concern. And that player is Jared Verse who, though he is still without a sack this season, is still a critical piece in the Browns' hopes to contain and attack veteran Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers. Verse is not expected to miss the big Week 8 game on Sunday, but his knee is giving him trouble and he sat out on Wednesday.

Asked about Verse's knee by reporters in Berea on Wednesday, coach Todd Monken shrugged off the severity of the problem.

Ask if Verse might sit out, Monken said, "I don't anticipate that. Just a little bit of swelling, and we just thought it'd be good to just keep him off of it."

Originally, the Browns listed four active players who were not practicing on Wednesday: CB Myles Harden (hamstring), RT Tytus Howard (concussion), C Elgton Jenkins (knee) and DE Jared Verse (knee).

But Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN posted an update once practice got rolling, adding, "Browns CB Myles Harden was actually on the practice field today.So was DT Mike Hall , who was practicing for the first time since injuring his ankle against the Steelers in Week 4.

Jared Verse Raised the Stakes for Browns-Steelers Showdown

Certainly, the expectation is that Verse would be on the field for the Steelers game, given the fact that he raised some eyebrows in suggesting the team played dirty during the Browns' Week 4 win in Cleveland. It would be a good time for the Browns edge rusher to get himself going–not only is he without a sack this season, but he has only four pressures this year.

Said Verse at the time: "They were talking crazy. I was telling them, 'You're double-teaming, y'all sliding, y'all garbage.' I was talking crazy to them. I don't have any respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra (expletive) after the game, excuse my French. So, I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a good time when I see them again."

articles.title: Aaron Danks reacts to Bayern's 6-1 win and provides Kompany update
articles.summary: Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks was pleased with his team's 6-1 victory over 1. FC Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal but acknowledged the challenges they...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks was pleased with his team's 6-1 victory over 1. FC Magdeburg in the DFB-Pokal but acknowledged the challenges they faced.

"It was a really good night for us. It was a difficult game. In the end, 6–1 is great, but before that, it felt very different. It was really difficult to press them. We had more control in the second half and had more options as well. I'm really happy, but it was by no means easy today ," Danks said.

The assistant coach also welcomed the news that Vincent Kompany had been discharged from hospital .

"Vincent is out of hospital. That's fantastic news. We're very pleased that he's getting better. But he needs to rest. He needs to recover, spend time with his family and continue to get better. He's doing better and is on the road to recovery. We'll simply try to do our best and prepare for the game on Saturday against Dortmund," Danks added.

articles.title: Napoli end wait for a win with strong second-half show at Monza
articles.summary: Napoli’s slow start to the season was finally given lift off after they thumped Serie A strugglers Monza 4-1 at Stadio Brianteo on Wednesday. Matteo Politano...
articles.body:
Napoli's slow start to the season was finally given lift off after they thumped Serie A strugglers Monza 4-1 at Stadio Brianteo on Wednesday.

Matteo Politano, Rafa Marín and Kevin De Bruyne produced second-half goals after the rivals entered the interval at 1-1.

Napoli took an 11th-minute lead when Giovanni Di Lorenzo rode a tackle as he charged out of defence and then produced a defence-splitting pass that was met with a magnificent finish by Rasmus Hojlund.

Gustavo Varela equalised two minutes before half-time with a well-taken glancing header made possible by Jay Robinson's mazy run and pinpoint cross.

Napoli's worst start to a season for 16 years looked set to continue but the visitors surged clear after the break.

Politano was the first to strike when Monza gave the ball away as they defended an attack down the right and the Italy winger reacted in a flash, driving into the area and finishing with a flourish.

Marin's glancing header from a corner in the 63rd minute opened up daylight and soon after De Bruyne put the result beyond doubt when he collected a pass from Noa Lang and sent his shot between the legs of keeper Noel Tornqvist.

Injury-ravaged Napoli felt the pressure lift from their shoulders and they pressed for a fifth with Lang causing problems down the left.

The victory lifts them to sixth in table with four wins from nine matches while Monza occupy 16th place, just two points above the relegation zone.

articles.title: Texans WR Jaylin Noel will miss rest of the season with turf toe injury
articles.summary: Houston Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel will miss rest of season with turf toe injury
articles.body:
Houston Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel is expected to miss the rest of the season and undergo surgery on his toe, a person with knowledge of the injury told the Chronicle.

Noel was place on the injured reserve because of turf toe, the team announced Wednesday afternoon.

The injury is a major blow, not only for the Texans, but also for Noel, who was off to a fast start and was leading the team with 331 receiving yards.

He also had 19 catches and two touchdowns.

The Texans drafted Noel in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft. The Texans do have depth at receiver after recently trading for Marvin Harrison Jr. and getting Tank Dell back from a significant knee injury.

This is a developing story. Check back later for updates.

articles.title: Lakeland's Kaydence Myers finishes 37th in state bowling. Here's how
articles.summary: Lakeland's Kaydence Myers finished 37th in the state bowling tournament. Here's how she pulled it off.
articles.body:
ORLANDO — Lakeland sophomore bowler Kaydence Myers wanted to zero in on her mark heading into the 2026 FHSAA State Bowling Championships, especially after what happened last year.

In 2025, Myers just missed the cut in districts to go to state. But this year she officially clinched her bid thanks to placing second in districts , registering a 560 series, which is a 186 average. Myers became the second Lakeland girl bowler to advance to state in the last three years. And in state, she racked up 37th out of 231 girls from around the state of Florida Tuesday, Oct. 28, 2026, at the Boardwalk Bowl and Entertainment Center in Orlando.

"I definitely finished much better than how I started. I went up by 50 pins the last two games, and I went up 40 places," Myers said.

Averaging a 180 in four games, Myers bowled a 157, 160, 207 and then a 193, which is a 717 total. And as evidenced, she missed her spares in the first two games but was able to capitalize on her marks the last two games.

The trend that happened to her that led to her doing better this year was her transition from a 12-pound ball to 14. Before, her 12-pound ball was going straight through the pins and not knocking as many down. At 14 pounds she is able to hit the pins harder because it carries more momentum and kinetic energy, deflecting less upon impact. As a result, her average upped from 160 in 2025 to 185 this year.

And her average increased in a year when she added a Thursday bowling league to her schedule while practicing for the Lakeland cheer team every day during the week.

"I do two cheer teams. It's definitely exhausting and then having to fit bowling into my spare time (is definitely a challenge)," Myers said.

"She will take what she learned today, and she will come back next year and do better," Lakeland bowling coach Thomas Kreamer said. "She's good. She did a lot better. She's more consistent on her approach with her walking and not stuttering and stopping with her steps. She's gotten more consistent. She (just) has to get more consistent and continue to carry the team like she's been doing all year. She's our No. 1 bowler. No. 1 bowler in Polk County. She's just going to continue to get better every day with her coming to the pro shop and coming to the bowling alley with me. ... She's going to continue to get better and up her scores even more."

For next year, Myers will return with Elizabeth Woodsby, who is the team's second-best bowler. And for the boys' team, all of the Dreadnaughts will be returning.

articles.title: Dodgers, Freddie Freeman Expected to Discuss Contract Extension This Offseason
articles.summary: Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman is entering the final year of his contract, and his future on the team will need clarity.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman is entering the final year of his contract, and his future will need some clarity soon.

Freeman is 37 years old and inching closer to 40. He has five years in the books with the Dodgers, and during that time he has delivered multiple big moments, while serving as the captain and helping the team win two World Series.

Dave Roberts and many players lean on Freeman's experience and leadership to guide them through tough times.

Freddie Freeman's contract status heading into the offseason

Freeman is in the last year of a six-year, $162 million contract that is paying him $27 million per season.

Now that his contract is coming to an end, the Dodgers and Freeman need to decide how they will proceed, in terms of how long his next deal will be and how much money he will pull in.

The California Post's Jack Harris believes the Dodgers and Freeman will discuss a new deal this offseason and how they will handle his final few seasons.

"Then there is Freddie Freeman, whose contract situation will come to a head over the next 12 months," Harris wrote.

"The 2027 season is the final one of Freeman's current deal. However, the 37-year-old has indicated a desire to potentially play at least two more seasons beyond it, putting the onus on the Dodgers to make a decision on his future in Los Angeles.

"To this point, the future Hall of Fame first baseman has repeatedly sidestepped any contract talk publicly. But it's unlikely next year begins without him and the team at least discussing his long-term status in the organization at some point."

The Dodgers, even as their team ages, will certainly want to keep Freeman, a quality contact hitter who offers good defense at first base.

Freeman's departure may unlock a path for some of their prospects to play, including Josue De Paula, since it is a position that a lot of players can play.

However, his value to the roster and clubhouse is so massive that they will ride it out with Freeman until he struggles.

During the All-Star break, Freeman laid out that he wants to play antoher three more years, reaching 40 years old.

"I've always wanted to try and play until I'm 40 years old," Freeman said. "That would be three more years after this. I'm not going to put a firm number on it. I would have to get another contract, so I'm only worried about this year. But 20 years in the big leagues would be kind of cool and special."

Freeman certainly wants to play and would love to play with the Dodgers. With the feeling being mutual on both sides, it is hard to see things working out any other way.

What will be interesting to see is the extact terms of the contract.

articles.title: Titans claim DT Jonah Laulu off waivers from Raiders
articles.summary: The Raiders won't have a chance to sign Jonah Laulu back to the practice squad. The former starter was claimed off waivers by the Titans.
articles.body:
This week was the deadline for the Raiders to activate WR Dont'e Thornton from injured reserve . And with that activation, they needed to make a corresponding move. It was former starting DT Jonah Laulu who was cut to make room, no doubt hoping he would clear waivers so they could bring him back onto the practice squad. Well, that is not going to happen.

Laulu was claimed off waivers by the Titans today, ending his tenure with the Raiders .

And with a practice squad spot open, the Raiders signed former Falcons third round EDGE Braden Trice instead.

Originally a round seven pick by the Colts in 2024, Laulu was waived at the end of his first training camp and claimed by the Raiders. He appeared in 39 games in Las Vegas since then, starting 22 of those games. He put up 91 tackles with 5.5 sacks, 11 tackles for loss, and 12 QB hits.

Laulu appeared in five games this season, but was inactive in Week 7 along with Thomas Booker IV in favor of second year man JJ Pegues. It was clear Laul had fallen out of favor with the new staff at a crowded position in need of a jolt. The top three at the position are Tonka Hemingway, Adam Butler, and Folorunso Fatukasi.

articles.title: 'We're all human': Tah opens up on Bayern's difficult week
articles.summary: A 6-1 victory might look comfortable on paper, but Jonathan Tah knows there is more to Bayern Munich's performance than the final score suggests. After Wedne...
articles.body:
A 6-1 victory might look comfortable on paper, but Jonathan Tah knows there is more to Bayern Munich's performance than the final score suggests. After Wednesday's DFB-Pokal win against 1. FC Magdeburg, the defender praised his team's patience, togetherness and ability to respond to a challenging situation.

"It's never easy, even though it looks like it from outside. It's always a lot of hard work. And the way our opponents tried to play today, they were brave. They tried to do things with the ball rather than simply sitting deep and hoofing it long. That's why we gradually found our rhythm, and at some point, the momentum shifted in our favour," Tah explained.

"Regardless of who's on the pitch, when I look at the players who came on towards the end, Daiber scoring the goal and Binder coming on, it shows that we stick together as a team and that everyone is ready to deliver when called upon. That's something you have to work for in training. It makes me happy to see that, despite having players missing and the coach being absent at the moment, we're still able to produce performances like this on the pitch," he added.

With head coach Vincent Kompany recovering at home after being discharged from hospital, Bayern have had to deal with an unusual situation.

"Well, I'd be lying if I said it didn't affect us in some way, because we're all human. Of course, you feel for those affected. But ultimately, I think it's about being professional. When you consider what we can do right now to give those who aren't here some positive energy, the answer is to go out on the pitch and show what we showed today. I'm pleased that we've managed to do that in each of our last two games," the defender said.

Former Bayern midfielder Bastian Schweinsteiger also asked Tah about the demands of playing in a defensive system that often leaves centre-backs exposed in one-on-one situations, and whether he would prefer an additional defensive midfielder for protection.

"Generally speaking, that's our style of play. We press high and, most of all, defend 1v1. As a defender, that sometimes means you have large spaces to cover. But, of course, the aim is that once you get into your own half, you can provide better cover for one another and avoid constantly finding yourself in 1v1 situations," Tah explained.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Aaron Danks gives positive update on Vincent Kompany
articles.summary: Aaron Danks gave FC Bayern the best health update on Vincent Kompany.
articles.body:
Over the past couple weeks, Bayern Munich assistant Aaron Danks has stepped up to offer some relief to Vincent Kompany while the man in charge dealt with various medical issues. After Kompany collapsed at the Bayern facility, Danks filled his absence by running the show in Bayern's 6-1 victory over FC Magdeburg in the second round of the DFB-Pokal.

In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Danks offered some very positive news on Vincent Kompany.

"Vincent is out of hospital," said Danks. "That's fantastic news. We're very pleased that he's getting better. But he needs to rest. He needs to recover, spend time with his family and continue to get better. He's doing better and is on the road to recovery. We'll simply try to do our best and prepare for the game on Saturday."

Danks will continue to operate as the manager. Bayern is also dealing with the absence of Joshua Kimmich due to a death in his family. The squad will be immediately lifted upon their respective returns but will also rely on the available players and coaches to remain as the only undefeated team in Europe.

articles.title: Bayern Munich dominant in 6-1 victory over FC Magdeburg
articles.summary: FC Bayern was brilliant in taking down FC Magdeburg.
articles.body:
If there was any doubt about Bayern Munich's intentions in the DFB-Pokal, the numbers from its 6-1 demolition of 1. FC Magdeburg should put those concerns to rest. Bayern didn't just win this one; it completely overwhelmed its opponent from beginning to end.

The Bavarians finished with 63% possession, outshooting Magdeburg 19-9 while putting eight attempts on target compared to just two for the hosts. The expected goals numbers were particularly eye-catching, with Bayern registering an enormous 3.98 xG against Magdeburg's 0.86. That is a massive difference in attacking quality and the opportunities created.

Perhaps the most telling statistic was touches inside the opposition penalty area. Bayern recorded an incredible 64 touches in Magdeburg's box, while the hosts managed just 11 in Bayern's. That's not simply territorial dominance; that's sustained pressure and an attacking performance that kept Magdeburg's defense under constant stress.

Bayern also created five big chances, converting four of them, while Magdeburg managed just one. The visitors completed 674 passes at 90% accuracy, compared to Magdeburg's 362 at 84%.

Magdeburg did manage to get nine shots away, but only two tested Bayern's goalkeeper. They also failed to earn a single corner, while Bayern won six.

The takeaway? This was Bayern operating at a completely different level. Six goals, nearly four expected goals, overwhelming possession, and relentless pressure in the attacking third.

The DFB-Pokal can be unpredictable, but Bayern made sure there would be no giant-killing story this time around. Magdeburg got its moment in the spotlight, but Bayern made it abundantly clear who was in charge.

articles.title: Thoroughbred Championship Series adds division for fillies; date set for 2027 Travers
articles.summary: The Oaks Division will carry a $1 million prize pool.
articles.body:
Churchill Downs Incorporated and the New York Racing Association announced Wednesday an expansion of their Thoroughbred Championship Series to include a separate division for 3-year-old fillies, and also revealed the 2027 dates for several of Saratoga Race Course's top races.

Most notably, the 2027 Travers Stakes will take place on Aug. 28. Won in 2026 by Leading Change, the Midsummer Derby is set to serve as the penultimate race in the now-named "Derby Division," which includes six races for 3-year-olds and was announced earlier this year.

That slate of Derby Division races, which also includes Saratoga's Jim Dandy, has the following schedule.

Kentucky Derby: May 1 at Churchill Downs Racetrack

Matt Winn Stakes: July 3 at Churchill Downs Racetrack

Jim Dandy Stakes: July 31 at Saratoga Race Course

Travers Stakes: Aug. 28 at Saratoga Race Course

TCS Championship: Sept. 25 at Churchill Downs Racetrack

The four-race Oaks Division for fillies has the following schedule.

Kentucky Oaks: April 30 at Churchill Downs Racetrack

Coaching Club American Oaks: July 24 at Saratoga Race Course

Alabama Stakes: Aug. 21 at Saratoga Race Course

The Oaks Division will carry a $1 million prize pool to be shared among the three highest-ranked horses in the final standings. The winner of the Oaks Division will also earn entry into the Sept. 25 TCS Championship Race and receive a bonus up to $1 million if she wins that race.

"The Oaks Division gives 3-year-old fillies a championship of their own, connecting four of the best races in the sport into one points race from Louisville to Saratoga," NYRA president David O'Rourke said in a news release. "And for the filly who comes out on top, it opens the door to take on the colts in September. It's a matchup fans have always wanted to see, and now there's a clear path to it."

Combined, the two horse racing series will offer more than $22 million in purses and prizes. Each of the 10 races will air on either NBC or Fox networks.

Previously, it was announced that the Derby Division will carry a $5 million prize pool.

articles.title: Short turnaround doesn’t give Packers rookie Trey Smack much time to iron out his form
articles.summary: Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack has missed seven kicks this year. Special teams coach Cam Achord said he needs to improve his contact with the ball.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY – Green Bay Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack will keep working on his foot strike to avoid another multi-miss game.

He just won't do it on the field until warmups before the Packers play the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night, Oct. 29.

Special teams coach Cam Achord said Smack needed to rest his leg because of the short turnaround between the Packers' loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday and the game against the Panthers .

Normally, Smack would practice field goals, extra points and kickoffs on Wednesday and then go through a lighter workout on Friday during a Sunday-to-Sunday game schedule. But with just three days between games, Achord preferred Smack not kick this week.

"During a game, you kick more than you do in practices, because every time you're driving, whether you're punting or kicking, once the ball gets close to midfield, you're in the kicking net kicking as a field goal kicker on the side," Achord said Oct. 28. "As soon as you get an offensive possession as a punter, you're getting something [started] because you don't know how fast we're going to go to huddle, you don't know how fast the possession is going to go.

"So, you may kick 100 balls potentially in a game on the side before you actually get [one] in the game, So, you kick so much on game day, you need the rest. I don't know if anyone actually in the league kicks on a short week. There may be one or two [teams]."

Smack has some work to do to correct his kicks.

He missed a chip shot wide right from 26 yards out in the first quarter and a 35-yarder wide right in the fourth quarter of the 20-17 loss to the Lions .

He has attempted 16 kicks this year and missed five field goals and two extra points. His .688 field goal percentage ranks tied for 29th and his .867 extra point percentage ranks 31st.

Smack has missed a kick in four games this year and two or more in two of his past three games.

"We've got to improve the contact," Achord said. "Like we've talked and it's even in pregame and different things. It's all about just the contacts. To me, it's how are we making contact with the football? What's it like coming off the foot?

"And that's what we've got to continue to work with, is getting the contact back to where it was and where it can be, which he's shown to have right multiple times and responded from things, you know, good and bad."

Lions defender D.J. Wonnum got a finger or two on Smack's 35-yard miss, but it's hard to tell whether it affected the ball's direction. Achord said it might have missed right even if it wasn't tipped.

"I think we've just got to continue to push forward, hit a better ball, obviously right there, and then we're not having the conversation," Achord said

Smack missed an extra point in the season opener against Minnesota but also hit a 59-yard field goal. He was perfect against the New York Jets, including a 26-yard walk-off field goal in overtime. He connected on a 58-yard field goal against Tampa Bay, but since then he's been 5-for-9 on field goals and 6-for-7 on extra points.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur has said he has no intention of abandoning his commitment to Smack and thinks the sixth-round draft pick will iron out his issues.

Achord said that he's not worried about Smack's mental state. He said he keeps reminding him that even if you go 9 of 10, people will remember the one miss, and that's not how he should see it.

His focus should remain on the process that allowed him to hit the other nine.

"You're going to have some ups and downs, but understand what got you here, what gets you to the point," Achord said. "It's doing that process over and over, and that's where you build the confidence, what you've done in the past to get you to where you are today, and that's what you have to have conversations about.

"A lot of people want to talk about the negatives and all that, which is fair. It's very fair. There's nothing wrong about that, but we've got to go back to the process that got us here and what we did 90% of the time."

articles.title: Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea (6-5 Pens): Reds Edge Dramatic Shootout to Reach Carabao Cup Quarter-Finals
articles.summary: Liverpool secured their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals following a dramatic penalty shootout victory over Chelsea at Anfield, with Wesley Fofana mis...
articles.body:
Liverpool secured their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals following a dramatic penalty shootout victory over Chelsea at Anfield, with Wesley Fofana missing the decisive spot-kick after the two sides had played out a 1-1 draw in normal time.

It was an evening of high drama on Merseyside as Andoni Iraola's Liverpool overcame Chelsea 6-5 on penalties to progress to the last eight of the competition. The visitors had taken the lead through a Morgan Rogers penalty before Cody Gakpo responded with a spot-kick of his own, ensuring the contest would ultimately be decided by a shootout.

The occasion also saw former Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso and ex-Reds captain Jordan Henderson return to Anfield with Chelsea, although neither enjoyed the outcome they had hoped for as the home side eventually prevailed.

Rogers and Gakpo Trade Penalties at Anfield

Chelsea made the breakthrough in the 40th minute when Morgan Rogers converted from the penalty spot, putting the visitors ahead in a closely contested League Cup encounter.

However, Liverpool's response was almost immediate, with Cody Gakpo stepping forward to level matters from 12 yards just three minutes later. The Dutch forward's equaliser restored parity before the interval and ensured that neither side would take a lead into the second half.

With a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the contest remained finely balanced as both teams searched for the decisive breakthrough. However, neither could find a winning goal during normal time, leaving penalties to determine which club would progress.

Dramatic Shootout Sees Chelsea Miss Their Chance

The shootout delivered several dramatic twists, with both sides struggling to establish a decisive advantage as the pressure increased.

Chelsea's Valentin Barco was among the first to falter, striking the woodwork with his attempt. Liverpool were unable to capitalise fully on that opportunity, however, as Kostas Tsimikas subsequently fired his effort over the crossbar.

Former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson then converted his penalty for Chelsea, adding another intriguing moment to his return to Anfield.

The visitors appeared to have gained a potentially decisive advantage when goalkeeper Mike Penders saved Ryan Gravenberch's effort, leaving Liverpool facing the prospect of elimination.

However, Giorgi Mamardashvili responded with a crucial save to deny Emmanuel Emegha, ensuring the shootout remained alive and handing Liverpool another opportunity to secure qualification.

Joe Gomez stepped forward to convert his penalty for the hosts, putting the pressure back on Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana.

The French international was unable to keep his effort on target, sending his spot-kick over the crossbar and bringing the shootout to a dramatic conclusion as Liverpool celebrated a 6-5 victory.

Chelsea Left to Reflect on Missed Opportunities

For Chelsea, the defeat represented a frustrating conclusion to an encounter in which they had opportunities to progress. Having taken the lead during normal time, the visitors were unable to preserve their advantage and ultimately saw their Carabao Cup campaign ended by a series of missed opportunities in the shootout.

Penders had briefly put Chelsea in a strong position with his save from Gravenberch, but Emegha's subsequent miss and Fofana's failure to convert proved costly.

The result also made for an unhappy return to Anfield for Alonso and Henderson. While the latter successfully converted his penalty against his former club, Chelsea were unable to secure the victory that would have taken them into the quarter-finals.

Liverpool Keep Their Carabao Cup Hopes Alive

For Liverpool, progression represents another positive result in their pursuit of domestic silverware, although the manner of victory highlighted just how narrow the margins can be in knockout football.

Gakpo's first-half equaliser ensured the hosts remained in contention, while Mamardashvili's intervention during the shootout proved particularly important in turning the contest back in Liverpool's favour.

Chelsea, meanwhile, must turn their attention to their remaining competitions after a disappointing exit that could easily have produced a different outcome.

Ultimately, the difference between the sides came down to composure in the decisive moments, with Liverpool surviving a turbulent shootout to secure their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.

The Reds advance to the last eight, while Chelsea's hopes of lifting the League Cup are over for another season.

articles.title: Patriots CB Carlton Davis shares major update on Week 8 injury status
articles.summary: Patriots veteran cornerback Carlton Davis is "ready to go" for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III intends to return from injury in Week 8 against the Miami Dolphins and is confident in his health with the game on the horizon.

According to Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller , Davis stated to the media how excited he is to have returned to practicing with the team in full swing ahead of the matchup.

"I'm ready to go," said Davis. "...It's going to be great having all the guys back. Being at full power and being able to go out there and feed off each other and make plays together."

Davis is preparing to return from a neck injury that has sidelined him for the last three weeks. His availability heading into Week 8 will provide a significant boost to New England's secondary as the unit prepares to contain the Dolphins' receiving corps.

Through three games played thus far this season, Davis has recorded 16 total tackles, a pass breakup and a tackle for loss. Those numbers reflect his contributions to the Patriots ' defense amid much time missed already this season.

The Dolphins' receiving unit is led by wide receivers Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell. articles.summary: Liam Scales provided a timely second-half goal to draw Celtic level in their Premiership clash with Dundee United.But it was still a frustrating night for th...
articles.body:
Liam Scales provided a timely second-half goal to draw Celtic level in their Premiership clash with Dundee United.

But it was still a frustrating night for the Hoops who weren't able to find a third goal on the night and had to be content with a share of the spoils after the game finished 2-2.

Camilo Duran gave Celtic the lead, but two quickfire goals from the visitors put them in front at the break.

Scales headed home from a Jota cross on 64 minutes, but despite laying siege to the Dundee United goal, they couldn't find a winner.Speaking to CelticPlayer after the game, the Irishman said: "I think we started the game quite well and then had a sloppy 10-15 minutes.

"We've dropped two points because of that, so it's disappointing, but I think we showed a lot of character in the second half to take control of the game.

"The ball just didn't drop for us at certain times in the box to go and finish the game off and get that winner."

The equaliser came from a quick corner, with Jota, on as a second-half substitute, firing in a dangerous ball which Scales met perfectly, steering his header beyond the Dundee United keeper.

And the defender is delighted to see the Portuguese winger back and playing an important role for the team.

"It's brilliant to have him back," he said. "You could tell how eager he is to play and to create and go by people.

"He really looks sharp and he's going to be massive for us now because we have so many games and we're going to need everyone and he's going to play a big part hopefully."

articles.title: Molineux mania! UP Warriorz outgun RCB in Rs 1.10 cr showstopper at WPL auction
articles.summary: UP Warriorz secured Australia captain Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 crore after a bidding battle with RCB at the WPL mini auction in Kochi. They also signed Gr...
articles.body:
KOCHI: UP Warriorz, with the biggest purse of Rs 3.75 crore, beat Royal Challengers Bengaluru in a fierce bidding war to sign Australia captain Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 crore at the WPL mini auction in Kochi on Wednesday. UP opened at Rs 50 lakh and RCB, for whom Molineux was part of the 2024 title-winning side, came straight back, and her price zoomed to Rs 95 lakh. UP then moved it to Rs 1 crore, the RCB countered at Rs 1.05 crore. UP finally pushed it to Rs 1.10 crore to seal the deal. Allrounder Molineux is the X-factor, who provides a wealth of experience for UP, and will be propped up as the perfect foil to her captain and compatriot, Meg Lanning. "We were determined to get Sophie at any cost," UP Warriorz CEO Kshemal Waingankar told reporters. "It puts us in a good position with Sophie and Grace (Harris) combined to tweak our combinations and decide what works best for us." UP added firepower to their batting by picking Australian Grace Harris for Rs 30 lakh, who returns to the franchise she represented in 2025. She had a prolific run in RCB's 2026 title season, but was released with Ellyse Perry's return. Harris is likely to open with Lanning or Pratika Rawal. With Harleen Deol also in the mix, it gives UP the legroom to mix and match their batters. "Grace brings power to the middle order, Molineux the leadership qualities," Waingankar added. They also snapped up experienced Himachal wicketkeeper Sushma Verma and bid Rs 30 lakh for offspinner Sneh Rana. With Sophie Ecclestone and Deepti Sharma in the squad, their spin attack looks robust. Unlike previous seasons, UP went into this auction with a clear plan. "We carried out some experiments last season that didn't work. This season, we were betting on experience, which is why we targeted players like Sushma Verma," UP head coach Abhishek Nayar said. Combinations were the priority for the five franchises, and with the other four on limited purse, the bidding remained largely cautious. Gunalan Kamalini, the young India batter with a high ceiling went to Gujarat Giants who made the first bid at Rs 40 lakh. RCB opened their account by snapping up Australian left-arm spinner Jess Jonassen at a base price of Rs 40 lakh. Mumbai Indians (MI) pursued Kiran Navigare, a former UP player, for a base price of Rs 40 lakh. Delhi Capitals took the price to Rs 75 lakh, and MI, with only Rs 90 lakh left in their purse, dropped out. Sri Lankan veteran Chamari Athapaththu going unsold was the biggest surprise of the evening. MI played it smart by picking childhood friends Disha Kasat and Latika Imandar, two players from Vidarbha who have been making waves at the domestic level, for Rs 10 lakh each. The auction's biggest takeaway was the continuing importance of domestic cricket to women's game, with franchises backing a raft of players who have emerged from the circuit.

Grace Harris (Rs 30 lakh, UP): Apart from her blistering strokeplay, she can bowl offspin in the Powerplay. Sushma Verma (Rs 30 lakh, UP): An international player currently in stellar form. Got exposure in the CPL. She walks into UP's playing XI given her keeping skills and experience. Disha Kasat (Rs 10 lakh, MI): An improved player from WPL 2023. She can be used as an opener. Kathryn Bryce (Rs 10 lakh, UP): Scotland captain, who can bowl medium pace and bat at the top of the order. Sanika Chalke (Rs 10 lakh, MI): Touted as the player of the future. Part of the 2025 U-19 T20 World Cup-winning squad. Samaira Raghav (Rs 10 lakh, GG): A16-year-old ex-sprinter who was pushed to cricket by her father. Currently making waves in Women's DPL.

UP Warriorz released Keralam leg spinner Asha Shobana for Rs 1.2 crore, then bagged her for a base price of Rs 30 lakh. Orla Prendergast became the first Irish cricketer to be picked in the WPL. The Gujarat Giants roped the allrounder for Rs 30 lakh.

articles.title: Paul Finebaum unsure about future at ESPN with expiring contract
articles.summary: Paul Finebaum is under contract with ESPN through this college football season, but the longtime radio host and college football analyst is unsure about his...
articles.body:
Paul Finebaum is under contract with ESPN through this college football season, but the longtime radio host and college football analyst is unsure about his future at the company.

Finebaum recently joined the Awful Announcing Podcast , where he confirmed ESPN pulled him from its programming last year after he told Clay Travis, then with OutKick, he was considering a run for U.S. Senate as a Republican. At the time, ESPN denied Finebaum was being sidelined. But one year later, Finebaum opened up about what he felt was an intentional sidelining by ESPN.

"Of course, I was sidelined," Finebaum said on the Awful Announcing Podcast . "I'd done the same shows every day for 13 years, and the next thing you know, I'm not on there after a college football weekend."

Finebaum ultimately returned to his regularly scheduled shows on ESPN and decided against a pivot to politics. But now his future at ESPN is in question again, with his contract set to expire next summer. Finebaum said he "feels pretty good" about his current relationship with ESPN, but that doesn't mean a new contract is imminent.

"I don't know yet," Finebaum admitted when asked whether he would like to stay at ESPN beyond this college football season. "The contract technically runs out in July, but I'm a college football analyst. So at the end of January, I will probably start contemplating exactly what is next. But I would be foolish to tell you anybody who is in the last year of a contract doesn't think about it. Troy Aikman thinks about it, so does everyone else. But I would also be foolish to tell you I know what I'm going to do next."

"I intend to continue doing what I'm doing, which is doing a show of some sort, but I don't know how it will be constructed," Finebaum continued. "These are always awkward situations that are probably best not discussed in the public airwaves, but then again, here we are."

Finebaum has been with ESPN since 2013, telling Awful Announcing he's not sure the company realized what they were getting with his radio show. "I don't think very many people at ESPN had ever listened to the show," Finebaum said. But even if they didn't know what they were getting, ESPN has been happy enough with the product to continue the partnership for more than a decade.

Aside from last year's sidelining, Finebaum's relationship with ESPN has been a successful one. He was integral in building SEC Nation , he continues to be a lead voice on college football for Get Up and First Take , and his radio show, which is simulcast on SEC Network, is one of the most popular in the country. If Finebaum is interested in staying with ESPN, the interest should be mutual.

articles.title: Man City 2-2 Brighton: Geronimo Rulli provides heroics but no worries for Gianluigi Donnarumma
articles.summary: Geronimo Rulli's penalty shootout heroics may have put the pressure on Gianluigi Donnarumma at Manchester City, but manager Enzo Maresca has no doubt about his number one.
articles.body:
Geronimo Rulli's penalty shootout heroics against Brighton in the Carabao Cup may have some questioning Gianluigi Donnarumma's spot at Manchester City, but manager Enzo Maresca has no doubt about his number one.

Rulli returned to the club in the summer from Marseille for a modest £1.7m to feature as a back-up to the Italy captain, but seemed to press his claims to challenge the jersey with an impressive display.

The 34-year-old dived full stretch to his left to save the last two penalties from Brighton's Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to allow holders City to progress to the quarter-finals of the competition.

The match had ended 2-2 in normal time and would not have gone all the way had Rulli not made a sensational fingertip save to deny Georginio Rutter in the second half.

Veteran Rulli will be back on the bench though for this weekend's Premier League game against the same opposition - despite Donnarumma's form being questioned by many in recent weeks.

When asked if Rulli had put pressure on Donnarumma's spot, Maresca told BBC Sport: "No, absolutely not from my point of view.

"He is working well but Rulli knows exactly his role, there is no doubt about that. Saturday it will be Gigio plus 10."

Holders Man City edge past Brighton on penalties

Man City's leaky defence highlights Donnarumma & Guehi struggles

Fleetwood to face Everton or Newcastle in last eight

Rulli is no stranger to being the hero in a penalty shootout.

In the 2021 Europa League final, he famously scored a penalty for Villarreal against Manchester United, before denying opposite number David de Gea to decide the marathon shootout and the destiny of the trophy.

If Rulli had not already ingratiated himself to City supporters with that moment against their rivals, then he will have rubberstamped the affection on Wednesday night.

The goalkeeper had spent the 2016-17 season at City without making a first-team appearance and returned to the club to replace James Trafford after the England international moved to Leeds for £45m.

It looks to be a canny piece of business from City.

In the pre-match news conference, Maresca said Rulli was "doing well" and "knows exactly his role" as understudy to Donnarumma, and that message was re-iterated after the game.

Along with Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol, Italian Donnarumma has been given three days off to "recover the energy" and Maresca will be hoping he returns to training this week rejuvenated.

Donnarumma was at fault for Aston Villa's second goal last weekend and Maresca acknowledged he has been "making some mistakes".

"Apart from penalties, overall he was good especially in the build-up," Maresca said of Rulli. "It was not easy because they are a team that go man to man and are aggressive.

"In the first half, we tried some long solutions with Floyd [Samba] and then in the second half we tried on the floor with Phil [Foden]. He made one good save and was good."

Big chance for City to go all the way again

Maresca shook up his starting line-up by making nine changes to the side that were beaten at Aston Villa on Saturday and it almost backfired.

City had twice fallen behind to goals from Malick Yalcouye and Georginio Rutter, but the hosts showed their battling spirit to draw level through Mateo Kovavic and Vitor Reis.

But the result continues Maresca's impressive start as manager, losing only against Villa and Paris St-Germain, as well as Arsenal in the Community Shield.

The Gunners were knocked out of the League Cup and so were Chelsea which means City will continue their quest to retain their trophy, coming up against Bradford in the quarter-finals.

Asked if it a big opportunity to go all the way again, Maresca said: "Absolutely.

"It's a different competition but the ambition has to be the same: this is a new project, new players, a new manager who started three months ago and we need to do our business and that is winning games.
