articles.title: Dream ownership group voices frustration in open letter over WNBA Finals venue concerns
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream released an open letter saying concerns over State Farm Arena availability for WNBA Finals Game 6 went unheeded for months.
articles.body: The logistics surrounding the WNBA Finals have drawn almost as much attention as the compelling, hard-fought action on the court. After negotiations reportedly described as "tense," the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries learned they would play Game 6 at State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta on Thursday. The game will tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET, making it a matinee on the East Coast and a breakfast-time start on the West Coast. Several Atlanta players downplayed the early start time, instead focusing on the task ahead. The Dream will look to keep their championship hopes alive and a find a way to force a decisive Game 7. Golden State took a 3-2 lead in the best-of-seven series Monday. The 12:30 p.m. ET tipoff drew mixed reactions, including from the Dream organization, which viewed the compromise as less than ideal. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In an open letter released Wednesday, the Dream suggested their concerns about finding a venue with enough capacity to host WNBA Finals games "did not receive the attention they deserved." The team also said that moving Game 6 to the early afternoon was "not what we fought for." Dream owners Larry and Robyn Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery said the team brought up concerns about potential scheduling conflicts months before the Finals started. "Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena," the letter stated. "As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved." All of Atlanta’s home playoff games this postseason have been played at State Farm Arena, the longtime home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks. The venue can accommodate roughly 17,000 fans. For the past several seasons, the Dream’s primary home court has been Gateway Center Arena, which holds a WNBA-low 3,500 spectators. The Dream recently announced plans to return to State Farm Arena for all home games beginning in 2027. The schedule changes have also affected the Hawks. Game 4 pushed Atlanta’s home game last Saturday against the Houston Rockets to 8:30 p.m., while Thursday’s Hawks-Cavaliers matchup will move to 8 p.m. to give arena crews time to prepare the building after the Dream-Valkyries game. WNBA FINALS GAME 6, A POTENTIAL TITLE-CLINCHER, WILL BE HELD IN THE AFTERNOON ON THURSDAY Game 3 was moved up one day, meaning all three WNBA Finals games played in Atlanta have needed some level of schedule adjustments. The ownership group also suggested the scheduling issues may have stemmed from an assumption Atlanta would not reach the Finals. "Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps, our place in the Finals was not accounted for. Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for its team." The Hawks also host the Miami Heat on Wednesday night, effectively ruling out an afternoon home game Thursday. VALKYRIES STARS TELLS FANS TO ‘CALL IN SICK’ FOR GAME 6 AS EARLY WNBA FINALS TIPOFF SPARKS FAN REACTION "As much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage," the letter continued. "That meant State Farm Arena." ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne described the decision to schedule Game 6 on a weekday afternoon as "the best of the bad solutions." Shelburne reported that moving Game 6 to Friday and Game 7 to Tuesday was among the options discussed. Tuesday, Nov. 3, is also Election Day for the midterm elections. The Golden State Warriors, who share Chase Center with the Valkyries, have home games scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 1, and Monday, Nov. 2. WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert praised the sellout crowds for Games 3 and 4 and welcomed more fans for Game 6. "The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we’re excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," Engelbert said in a statement on Monday. "We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta." The WNBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, NBA and broadcast partners held discussions over the weekend as they worked to find a solution, according to ESPN. Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens urged employers and educators to "extend a little grace" to Dream fans on Thursday afternoon. "Whether they’re at the game or catching a few moments on their devices, please allow them to be excited for our home team," he wrote in a social media flyer. The Calgary Flames are taking on the bitter provincial and divisional rival Edmonton Oilers in the first Battle of Alberta for the 2026-27 NHL season, and the Flames are looking to continue their recent hot streak of play.

However, they were dealt a worrying piece of injury news when they lost one of the players most responsible for their upswing.

Following a collision with Colton Dach, Flames goaltender Devin Cooley has departed the game, and has departed the game.

Calgary Flames Goaltender Devin Cooley Injured During Battle of Alberta Against Oilers

During the first period of play, Cooley was injured when Edmonton's Colton Dach collided hard with him while driving to the net.

Dach received a minor penalty for the infraction, while Cooley was slow to recover. To begin the second period, backup Dustin Wolf was between the pipes for Calgary.

Wolf, who has won four starts in a row, has amassed a 4-2-0 record this season with a 2.67 goals-against average and a .915 save percentage.

Devin Cooley Is In His Second Season With The Flames

Cooley began his junior career with the San Jose Jr. Sharks before playing for the Muskegon Lumberjacks, Springfield Jr. Blues and Wenatchee Wild. He then spent three seasons at the University of Denver, recording six shutouts, a .927 save percentage and a 1.93 goals-against average in 32 games.

Cooley signed with the Nashville Predators after college and spent most of the 2020-21 season with the Florida Everblades before playing the next two years primarily with the American Hockey League affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. He signed with the Buffalo Sabres before the 2023-24 season and started with the AHL's Rochester Americans, going 3-0-1 before receiving an emergency NHL recall.

Buffalo traded Cooley to the San Jose Sharks for a 2025 seventh-round pick on March 8, 2024. He made his NHL debut against the Chicago Blackhawks on March 17 and earned his first NHL win days later, beating the St. Louis Blues.

Cooley signed a two-year contract with the Flames in 2024; he was re-signed to a two-year extension with a $1.35 million salary cap hit.

articles.title: Takeaways from the Chicago Bulls’ loss to the Knicks, including a spark between Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson
articles.summary: For years, the Chicago Bulls have been waiting on a one-two punch. In the second quarter of Wednesday’s 133-127 loss to the New York Knicks at the United Cen...
articles.body:
For years, the Chicago Bulls have been waiting on a one-two punch.

In the second quarter of Wednesday's 133-127 loss to the New York Knicks at the United Center, Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis delivered it.

It started with a right hook. Jordan Clarkson caught Buddy Hield overcorrecting at the arc and took a straight-line drive to the basket. Wilson met him there, timing his jump to match the guard at the peak of his trajectory and smack the ball away with his right hand. Hield grabbed the rebound and flipped it up to Wilson. The rookie took one dribble, two more steps and then lofted a pass in a deft parabola to find the hands of Buzelis.

Buzelis had been struggling. Again. He started this season a little off key, never finding the right harmony to complement Wilson as the melody of the team. He overshot his dunk attempts, missed wildly on blocks, fumbled passes out of bounds. But against the Knicks, the pair finally struck the same chord. And when Buzelis grabbed that pass out of the air, double-clutching on his way to a dunk, the Bulls could hear for a moment the tune of a new future for this team.

For the first four games of this season, Wilson has stood out — albeit through immense growing pains — while Buzelis tried to figure out his role as a complementary piece. It's not an immediate fit. Wilson plays roughly the same position as Buzelis, although he is already slightly longer and heftier than the third-year forward. His arrival has scaled Buzelis down on the rotation chart, requiring him to guard backcourt players and take on a higher load of ball-handling and facilitation responsibilities.

This is a learning experience Buzelis has welcomed. But he gets frustrated. Understandably so. He was benched in the fourth quarter of Chicago's first win of the season. At times in the first four games of the year, it felt as if the Bulls played their most winning basketball when Buzelis was not on the court. Aspects of that frustration seeped into Wednesday's loss. Buzelis stepped on the line twice before shooting — and making — two separate 3-pointers, earning a whistle and a turnover. He airballed a 3-pointer in clutch time. He scored only two points in the fourth quarter.

But that moment of connection between Buzelis and Wilson was enough to refresh excitement around the pair's future together for the Bulls. Wilson scored 20 points. Buzelis scored 17. The pair closed the game together. And while the Bulls fell six points short of their intended goal, they took a step toward establishing a stronger long-term partnership between their most important pairing.

"Matas is my guy off the court and on the court," Wilson said. "I love playing with him. He had a great game tonight and I'm excited to see him keep flourishing and getting better every night. I want to connect on a bunch more lobs both ways. I just feel like it's a step in the right direction."

Here are three more takeaways from the loss.

It takes pure effort to unseat a team from its throne. Early in the second quarter, the Bulls determined exactly how many joules of exertion it took to rise to that challenge.

OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns went crashing to the ground and the Bulls went racing to the other end of the court. Josh Giddey took a 3-pointer in transition, then tore off the moment the ball left his hand in pursuit of the rebound. Matas Buzelis beat him to the punch, tearing the ball out of the air and jamming it back into the basket with a dunk.

The Knicks called a timeout the moment the basket was scored. The Bulls needed it, too. They were gassed, players gasping with the exertion of trying to run the Knicks out of their gym. But that effort was exactly what it took for the 1-3 Bulls to edge out ahead of the Knicks, who are suffering a slow start of their own this season. A buzzer-beater 3-pointer from Tre Jones put the Bulls up 62-56 to enter the second half, earning a thunderous — and almost surprised — roar from the crowd.

The Bulls led by as many as 19 points, but the Knicks chipped away at that deficit with the steady assurance of a high-powered team with plenty of winning under its belt. Jalen Brunson took decisive control in the fourth quarter, crossing up Powell so violently that he almost sent the veteran fully to his knees on one play and slinging three 3s in the final quarter alone. Landry Shamet and Jordan Clarkson also lit up on offense off the bench, combining for six 3s.

The ultimate backbreaker for the Bulls, however, was something familiar — second chances. The Knicks doubled the Bulls on the offensive boards over the entire course of the game. And they secured three of those offensive rebounds in the final quarter, scoring six second-chance points that ultimately determined the final differential.

Bulls coach Tiago Splitter wanted to let his team play free in the clutch, opting to forego a timeout to draw up a play when Giddey secured a rebound with 24 seconds left and the Bulls trailing by only three points. The ensuing off-the-cuff play resulted in a missed 3 by Powell.

"I thought we could get a good shot when they were not set and they were not with the matchup they liked," Splitter said. "I thought we could get something out of it. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Today it didn't work."

"And now of course I regret not calling timeout," Splitter added with a wry smile.

The bad luck had to end at some point. The Bulls were the worst shooting team in the entire NBA through their first four games, going only 40-for-168 (23.8%) from deep in that span. But against the Knicks, the drought finally broke. The Bulls went 18-for-42 from behind the arc, led by four 3s from Norman Powell and a trio apiece from Wilson, Buzelis and Jalen Smith.

The Bulls are unlikely to shoot above 42% very often this season, but this course correction shows their original shooting slump isn't an accurate encapsulation of the team's shooting ability. Continued strong shooting from Wilson and Buzelis will be crucial for the Bulls to sustain their scoring.

articles.title: Bulls Coach Tiago Splitter: 'We Got Better Tonight' in Loss to Knicks
articles.summary: Chicago may have lost to the defending champion New York Knicks, but the Bulls' head coach seemed pleased with the effort from young stars Matas Buzelis and...
articles.body:
Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson speaks to the media following his team's 133-127 loss to the New York Knicks on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Gavin Dorsey/Roundtable Sports)

The Bulls don't count moral victories, but head coach Tiago Splitter recognizes that his young team is improving.

Going against the defending champion New York Knicks on Wednesday night, Chicago played its best game yet this season. Although the Bulls lost, 133-127, Splitter's group had its most assists, fewest turnovers and best shooting percentage in the first five games. The team played collectively, rather than as a group of individuals, and it nearly resulted in the upset. However, the Bulls were outscored in the fourth quarter, 43-31.

"We were focused for a longer period of time throughout the game, which is good, but the game still has 48 minutes," Splitter said. "That last quarter tonight wasn't good enough. Of course, they have great players... That's why they won the championship. But I think we competed for the most part. We got better tonight."

After shooting a league-worst 23.8% on three-pointers through the first four games, the Bulls connected on 18 of their 42 shot attempts (42.9%) from beyond the arc. Norman Powell made four triples, while Matas Buzelis and No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson — who both struggled with accuracy to start the year — each made an efficient three shots from deep.

Buzelis, 22, and Wilson, 20, are Chicago's two highest draft picks over the past three years. Both are close in size and play similar roles, but haven't quite found a fit alongside each other. Wednesday's game was a strong outing for the young duo, who combined for 37 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks.

"I think they play better together," Splitter said. "And also, when they were not together, they were aggressive, trying to make plays, take care of the ball. We still got too many turnovers there sometimes, gotta be smarter in some situations. But again, I can go to sleep if we fight like this and compete every night."

Midway through the second quarter, Wilson blocked Knicks guard Jordan Clarkson at the rim, then took the ball the other way in transition. From just inside the three-point line, the rookie forward lobbed a pass to Buzelis, who threw down the alley-oop jam. It was the first such connection between the two players this season.

Buzelis and Wilson are widely expected to be the future of Chicago Bulls basketball. Although both can be prone to mistakes this early in their careers, the excitement they can generate was on display on Wednesday night.

"Matas is my guy, off the court and on the court," Wilson said. "I love playing with him. He had a great game tonight, and I'm excited to see him keep flourishing and getting better every night. I want to connect on a bunch more lobs both ways. I just feel like it's a step in the right direction. I know Coach said there's no moral victories, but I feel like we're definitely heading the right way."

The Bulls are in the midst of a brutal early-season stretch of the schedule, in which they play 10 consecutive games against teams that made the playoffs last season. Games against the Celtics and the Knicks put Chicago 20% of the way through the gauntlet, which provides learning experiences for the Bulls' young roster.

Chicago will head to Boston again on Friday for a rematch against the Celtics, then will continue the road trip against the Philadelphia 76ers before playing the Knicks again. The 10-game stretch also includes matchups with the San Antonio Spurs, the Atlanta Hawks, the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Cleveland Cavaliers.

articles.title: Sartell boys soccer advances to State Semifinals for first time in program history
articles.summary: The Sabres are advancing to the Class 2A State Semifinals for the first time in program history and are riding the confidence of 18 consecutive wins.
articles.body:
MONTICELLO, Minn. — When the Sartell boys soccer team last stepped onto the field at Monticello High School, the Sabres left in heartbreak. They were determined to not relive those feelings this go around, beating Orono 2-1 in an overtime thriller for their 18th-consecutive victory.

"I've wanted this moment to come back around ever since that day," senior forward and captain Cole Davidson said. "I've been working ever since, and I just knew it'd be back. It's an amazing feeling."

Coming out of halftime in a scoreless stalemate, freshman Nolan Guzman got the breakthrough goal in the 34th minute of the second half to give Sartell the lead.

After 33 minutes of tireless defensive effort, and a few strong looks on goal, that 1-0 lead stayed true until senior Mason Revering scored in the final seconds of the game to force overtime for Orono.

"You got to regroup and control what you can control," head coach Caleb Forberg said. "The message before overtime was to end it early."

Following such a gut-punch at the end of regulation, senior midfielder Ashton Shosted drew a penalty kick just two minutes into the overtime period. After selecting Davidson to take the kick, Forberg knew the PK was going in before the ball was even kicked.

"There was no doubt in my mind on the sideline that he was going to put that one in," Forberg said. "There's excitement and relief. I know these guys are going to remember that, and so will I. It's all you can ask for out of your senior group."

This senior group has been one to remember for the Sabres, registering four consecutive winning seasons and improving from 8-7-1 as sophomores to now 18-2-0 as seniors.

To return to the same field of heartbreak a year ago, with a bulk of the same roster on the field, is a testament to the grit and dedication this senior class bestows within themselves.

"The boys stuck to the plan," Forberg said. "We talk about it every practice. Just stick with it, [don't] ride the highs and the lows. We were low at the end of this game, but we can't ride it. It's a credit to the guys to be able to get on each other in a positive way."

It is the first time in program history that Sartell is making it past the State Quarterfinal and is guaranteed to max-out the number of games played in a single season.

"That's been the goal ever since last year, it's a big deal," Davidson said. "I've grown really great bonds with all these boys, and it means a lot to get this far with them. It's amazing."

Sartell will take on Cretin-Derham Hall at 2:30 p.m., Wednesday, Nov. 4 at U.S. Bank Stadium in hopes of keeping its win streak alive.

With a win, the Sabres would advance to the championship scheduled for 2:45 p.m., Saturday, Nov. 7 at U.S. Bank. With a loss, they would play in the third-place game at noon, Thursday, Nov. 5 at West St. Paul Regional Athletics Center.

"It's an amazing feeling; I've known these boys for a long time," Forberg said. "Eighteen wins is an amazing accomplishment, but it is one game at a time and that's the message. We're going to go down to U.S. Bank on Wednesday and we're going to give it our all. We can still control our destiny."

articles.title: Republic FC’s Kyle Edwards making history as Sacramento prepares for playoffs
articles.summary: SACRAMENTO, Calif. (KTXL) — Sacramento Republic FC forward Kyle Edwards has developed a reputation for delivering when his team needs him most. Whether it’s...
articles.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. (KTXL) — Sacramento Republic FC forward Kyle Edwards has developed a reputation for delivering when his team needs him most.

Whether it's a late-game goal, a burst of energy off the bench or a game-winning finish, Edwards has become one of Republic FC's most valuable weapons heading into the USL Championship playoffs.

"He's like a secret weapon. Although he's not so secret, but he's still very hard to stop," Republic FC head coach Neill Collins said.

Edwards finished the regular season with seven goals in the final 15 minutes of matches, the most in the USL Championship. Four of those goals were game-winners.

He also set a new league record with nine regular-season goals as a substitute, breaking his own mark of eight established in 2025. On September 26, Edwards also became the USL Championship's all-time leader in career regular-season goals scored off the bench.

For Edwards, the records are rewarding, but the moments behind them mean even more.

"It feels good. But I also know, like it's part of my job," Edwards said. "I'm happy that these goals come at very crucial times, and we can all celebrate it as a team and as fans and as a club as a whole."

His ability to deliver in critical moments has made him a difference-maker for Sacramento. Edwards also became just the fifth player in Republic FC history to score at least 10 goals in his first season with the club.

But his impact extends beyond the scoresheet.

"We always know, like, if we're not playing good or behind, we know we have him on the bench who can bring a massive spark," teammate Blake Willey said. "And he always finds a way to deliver."

It's a role Edwards has embraced throughout his first season with Republic FC, understanding that his contributions aren't always measured by goals.

"Even if I don't score, I just got to bring the energy because that's something I can control," Edwards said.

And when he does find the back of the net, there's a personal tradition that has become part of his celebrations.

Edwards often pulls out a headband he keeps around his waist and puts it on after scoring. The message reads "100% Jesus," a tribute to the faith he says has guided his journey.

"He blessed me with the talent, so I got to give back to him in any way possible," Edwards said. "And what more better way to give back to him than, you know, celebrating with him, scoring a goal."

Edwards credits his upbringing and his mother, who raised him alongside his two brothers and sister, for shaping the person he has become. He also credits his teammates for helping him grow both on and off the field.

Now, his focus shifts to the postseason, where Republic FC hopes to build on its regular-season success.

Following a dramatic final night of regular-season play, Sacramento enters the USL Championship playoffs as the Western Conference's No. 2 seed and will host seventh-seeded FC Tulsa on Sunday, November 1.

For Edwards, the opportunity to compete for a championship is exactly what brought him to Sacramento.

"I think adding the next star to the badge has been my number one goal," Edwards said. "And it still is."

Republic FC won its first league championship in 2014. Now, Edwards hopes to help bring another title to Sacramento.

Sunday's playoff match against FC Tulsa kicks off at 6 p.m. at Heart Health Park. Tickets are available at SacRepublicFC.com .

articles.title: Cowboys Delay Injury Decision on $33 Million Star
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys shelled out for safety Jalen Thompson in free agency. Will he finally get back on the field? The post Cowboys Delay Injury Decision on $33...
articles.body:
It had been 14 years since the Dallas Cowboys, a team notably wary of paying out money in NFL free agency, had given out the kind of contract that was given to safety Jalen Thompson this winter, a three-year, $33 million deal to bolster the back end of the defense. Thompson played three games before he injured his hamstring, badly enough that he has been on injured reserve since. But his four weeks are up, which means the Cowboys are eligible to open the practice window on Thompson.

They would then have 21 days to activate Thompson, or would have to move him to the season-long injured reserve. But to open the week of practice, the Cowboys have not indicated that they're going to make that move on Thompson.

Cowboys Still Unsure About Jalen Thompson Return

For a Cowboys team that thought it had loaded up on safeties coming into the year, getting Thompson back would be big, because the depth has not panned out quite the way the team had hoped–PJ Locke has been injured, out with a torn plantar fascia (he is set to return), and rookie Caleb Downs has been more of a slot corner than a safety, at least when everyone is healthy.

In setting the stage for the Cowboys practice week, coach Brian Schottenheimer laid out who was available. From Tommy Yarrish of the team website: " Cowboys LB Dee Winters (calf) and S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) worked with director of rehab Britt Brown on the resistance cords today. Thompson, who has been on IR since September 30, has missed 4 games and can have his 21-day practice window opened. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said yesterday the team had 'not yet' made a decision on opening his window."

Thompson, then, is highly unlikely to be back this week. But the Cowboys can start ticking off days until he gets there.

articles.title: Knicks’ Jalen Brunson shares special moment with Derrick Rose after NY win over Bulls
articles.summary: The New York Knicks continued their resurgence after losing the first three games of the season with a 133-127 victory over the Chicago Bulls. Jalen Brunson...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks continued their resurgence after losing the first three games of the season with a 133-127 victory over the Chicago Bulls. Jalen Brunson was once again the star of the night, producing 38 points and seven assists in a game that saw them trail by as many as 19 points in the second half.

Brunson, who helped New York notch up their second straight win after previously starring in the game against the Detroit Pistons, found the time post-game to share a moment with none other than Derrick Rose . The 30-year-old was joined by his father Rick as the two walked over to Rose and dapped him up before sharing a hug, per a post on X by SNY Knicks.

The Knicks were under plenty of pressure after opening the season with a 1-3 record. However, the offence once again came to the fore as Karl-Anthony Towns produced a double-double of 19 points and 13 rebounds. OG Anunoby scored 23 points off 7-16 shooting and also had six rebounds 31 minutes while Jordan Clarkson and Landry Shamet provided plenty of support off the bench.

Clarkson finished the game with 18 points and grabbed three boards while Shamet had 14 points and five assists. The Bulls, meanwhile, slumped to their fourth loss in five games and led by six points at the start of the fourth quarter.

However, New York opened with a 10-2 run and increased their lead to 10 points with almost four minutes left on the clock. Chicago fought back to bring the game back to within three points with 46 seconds remaining, but Brunson and Anunoby ended up stealing the game at the end.

Chicago were led by Norman Powell with 30 points with 10-15 shooting while Jalen Smith had a double-double of 17 points and 11 rebounds. They will now travel to Boston to take on the Boston Celtics, while the Knicks will host the Philadelphia 76es on Friday.

articles.title: Giants hand Devils first home defeat of EIHL season
articles.summary: Cardiff Devils suffer their first home defeat of the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) season as Belfast Giants claim a 4-1 win at Vindico Arena.
articles.body:
Cardiff Devils suffered their first home defeat of the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) season as Belfast Giants claimed a 4-1 win at Vindico Arena.

The Devils had boasted a 100% home record across 14 league, cup, and pre-season matches in 2026-27.

After a goalless first period Belfast scored twice in the second through David Goodwin on the powerplay and Scott Conway.

Logan Cockerill extended the visitors' lead early in the third, before Thomas Caron claimed his first Devils goal.

However, the Giants restored their three-goal advantage with a Kaleb Pearson penalty shot.

"With and without the puck, everything was tedious and looked like really hard work," said Devil's head coach Paul Thompson.

"Take nothing away from Belfast they totally deserved the win and we just couldn't get it going."

Cardiff remain top of the EIHL standings, with nine points from six games before hosting Guildford Flames on Saturday, 31 October.

The Welsh club have also been confirmed as Challenge Cup semi-finalists following Sheffield Steelers 5-2 win against Manchester Storm.

However, Devils back-to-back Cup wins last weekend - 4-2 at Nottingham Panthers and 1-0 at home to Steelers - could explain his side's lack-lustre showing against Belfast according to Thompson.

"I don't make excuses and I think our fans know that," added the veteran coach.

"I mean we're deeply disappointed but I know I pushed a lot of players and played a lot of players a lot of minutes last weekend and today we just looked like we didn't have any jump.

"We were second to every puck and I know my own team, and I know how they can perform, and we weren't even at 50% of where I think that was and maybe the weekend took more out of us than I thought it would."

articles.title: Viera punches ticket to final four, Satellite eliminated
articles.summary: Satellite finished as the Class 4A, Region 2 runner-up after a defeat at Bishop Moore while Viera beat Gateway to advance to the 5A state semifinals.
articles.body:
ORLANDO — For the third time this season, Satellite traveled to Bishop Moore looking to break through against the Hornets in the Class 4A, Region 2 final.

The Scorpions struggled from the jump as Bishop Moore overwhelmed them with their all-around strong play in a 25-8, 25-12, 25-20 win for the Hornets.

"Not our best. Bishop Moore played lights out," Satellite head coach Daren Bolton said. "I'm not going to take anything away from them. I don't know if we played our best match if we would have won it, but it was a little disappointing how we played but not disappointing season. I'm proud of this team."

It was the first regional final for all the players on the court as Satellite hadn't been in this position since 2021. The nerves were on display early as it finished the first set with more errors (nine) than points scored (eight).

"This team, for as young as it, all season I kept waiting and thinking the moment would overwhelm them. It never has and I would say definitely a little bit (tonight). We were a little bit overwhelmed," Bolton said. "Bishop Moore came out strong. We didn't answer, but I'm hoping that this is an experience for this program. We had a lot of kids here in our program experiencing this so that the next time they're in this situation, they should be better prepared."

Bishop Moore put together a clinical performance as it clinched its third regional title in four years. The Hornets ended the night with 37 kills, nine blocks and five aces.

"They passed incredible, but we didn't serve as well as we did the previous time we played them. We weren't aggressive in all phases of the game," Bolton said. "We got a little predictable on offense. They got too good of a block to be predictable on offense. It all started with our ball control. We weren't controlling the ball to be able to run our offense that we normally run."

Scorpions sophomore Harper Lanza led the team with seven kills. Sophomore Kenzie Little produced five kills and senior Lily Ruda finished with four kills and one ace.

Satellite puts a bow on a successful 22-7 season. The Scorpions won 18 of their final 21 matches with three defeats coming against Bishop Moore twice and Merritt Island.

They feature a talented young core in Lanza, Little, junior Lily Sigety, sophomore libero Cady Tinch and junior middle Macy Ferland.

"This season was amazing. I'm proud of our finish. I'm just proud of this team how they performed night in and night out. Even the character they showed (tonight) to not quit," Bolton said. "They didn't lay down. They could have laid down and just got overwhelmed. They fought and that's all a coach can ask for."

Seven seniors played their final high school volleyball match in Ruda, Azalea Miller, Raina Aldridge, Leigh Hertel and Kirra Snyder.

"This senior class is the most selfless group I've ever had. I had three seniors that didn't play a lot, but they worked their butts off in practice and pushed the starters. I got the best bench, period," Bolton said. "This is a team of selfless players that everybody just accepted their role, worked hard, ready to step in when needed but also ready to work hard every day in practice."

The regional final marked the final match for Bolton as Satellite's head coach. He is stepping down after 17 seasons as a head coach.

"It's been amazing. The No. 1 thing is the relationships I've developed, the kids I've been able to coach, the support of the administration, the support of the community," Bolton said. "This program is on the rise. It's going to get nothing but stronger. I feel great of where it's being left in and what the future holds."

(4) Viera def. (2) Gateway 3-2 (25-20, 26-28, 25-22, 20-25, 15-13)

In a back-and-forth regional final, Viera prevailed to punch their first final four ticket since 2023. Gateway saved five match points in the fifth set before junior Addi Casey spiked the title-clinching kill off a Panthers block.

The Hawks will compete in the Class 5A state semifinals on Nov. 5 at Polk State College in Winter Haven.

articles.title: Lakers, playing without Luka Doncic, have others step up in win over Clippers
articles.summary: Collin Sexton and Jarred Vanderbilt come through for the Lakers in their 16-point victory over the Clippers.
articles.body:
Lakers scoring phenom Luka Doncic missed his first game of the young season with back tightness, leaving a giant hole in their offense with the NBA's leading scorer (36 points per game) sitting out.

Lakers defensive star Ziaire Williams also missed his first game with left foot soreness, leaving them even more depleted with two starters unable to play.

The Lakers added a lot of depth over the summer in case of injury situations and now it was going to be tested against the Clippers at Intuit Dome.

Collin Sexton is one of the players the Lakers acquired for a moment like Wednesday, and he delivered in a big way, coming off the bench to provide energy and effort in helping the Lakers take a 103-87 victory over the Clippers.

Sexton was at his best in the third quarter, scoring 11 of his 21 points, flexing and pounding his chest after a made basket. His play helped the Lakers open a 22-point lead they never lost.

He was four for five from the field in the third, six for 11 for the game. He was two for three from three-point range in the third, four for seven for the game. He also had four rebounds and two assists.

Quentin Grimes (23 points), Matisse Thybulle (15) and Austin Reaves (16 points) did their part to help the Lakers improve to 4-1 .

Doncic and Williams played against the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday night at Crypto.com Arena, but they couldn't go in the back-to-back game.

"Both those guys woke up with some soreness and tightness today — tightness for Luka, soreness for Ziaire," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. "We have a tough stretch of games. Not a lot of time between [games so] just being overly cautious."

The Lakers next play at the Golden State Warriors on Friday, their fourth game in six days.

Redick was asked if Doncic and Williams would be available for that game.

Redick turned to Jarred Vanderbilt, who didn't play in the first four games, and Jaden Hardy, who played in the first game of the season, to help the shorthanded Lakers in their time of need. Vanderbilt played 21 minutes and had seven rebounds. Hardy played nine minutes and had two points.

"Yeah, I go back to something I said a couple of times already is that every guy's going to get an opportunity throughout the season," Redick said. "...Guys that haven't played are going to get opportunities tonight."

The Clippers, however, have their own injuries to worry about.

Clippers forward Rui Hachimura (left quad soreness) missed his first game of the season, joining Bradley Beal (right knee injury management), Brandon Ingram (right heel surgery), Jordan Miller (left rotator cuff surgery), Yanic Konan Niederhauser (right lisfranc surgery) and Max Strus (right plantar fascia partial tear) on the injury report.

The Lakers signed center Lawson Lovering to a two-way contract Wednesday and waived two-way forward AK Okereke.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Michigan vs. Rutgers Over/Under: Predictions for the Wolverines
articles.summary: Michigan has plenty of questions to answer heading into its matchup against Rutgers. Here are some Over/Under predictions involving the Wolverines' quarterba...
articles.body:
Michigan heads to Rutgers this weekend looking to get back on track after another frustrating offensive performance against Indiana. With questions surrounding the quarterback position, the struggling offensive line and an inconsistent rushing attack, there are plenty of intriguing storylines to watch. Here are five Over/Under predictions for the Wolverines against the Scarlet Knights.

1. Bryce Underwood Offensive Snaps — 3.5

The quarterback situation remains one of Michigan's biggest storylines. Tommy Carr replaced Underwood against Penn State and started against Indiana, but the offense still hasn't found much success. Unless Carr struggles significantly or Michigan builds a comfortable lead, Underwood could spend another Saturday watching from the sideline. He played just two snaps against Indiana last weekend.

If Michigan can't run the football against Rutgers, when will it? The Scarlet Knights rank No. 128 nationally against the run giving up 199.14 yards per game, presenting a golden opportunity for Jordan Marshall, Savion Hiter and Michigan's struggling offensive line. Kyle Whittingham wants a physical rushing attack, and this matchup should provide an opportunity to establish one.

This one piggybacks off No. 2. Hiter is averaging just over nine totes per game this year but he needs at least 10 carries against the Scarlet Knights. Marshall figures to remain heavily involved, but Hiter should receive plenty of opportunities against a vulnerable Rutgers defense. Michigan desperately needs explosive plays, and Hiter possesses the talent to provide them. If the Wolverines commit to running the football, double-digit carries for the freshman seem realistic.

Marsh has the talent to be a 5+ receptions guy each week, but it's only happened twice this year (UTEP, Iowa). JJ Buchanan emerged as Bryce Underwood's favorite target, so it'll be interesting to see if that changes at all if Carr remains under center. Marsh can definitely still be an important weapon in Michigan's passing attack, but opportunities could be limited this week if the Wolverines establish the run. Marsh could make an impact without necessarily catching five passes.

Michigan's offensive struggles have been well documented, but Rutgers represents an opportunity for a much-needed breakthrough. The Wolverines should be able to establish the run, create manageable passing situations and sustain drives. If Michigan can't score at least 25 points against this opponent, the pressure on offensive coordinator Jason Beck will only intensify. The Wolverines are currently averaging just 20.3 points per game, which puts them at No. 118 in the country. Kyle Whittingham constantly talks about Jason Beck's track record and how good he's been in the past, but at this point, it's a "what have you done for me lately" situation. He's now seven games into his Michigan career — it's time to forget about the success at Utah.

articles.title: Kevin Cash Explains Why He Pulled Drew Rasmussen Early in Rays World Series Loss
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash explained his decision to pull Drew Rasmussen after four innings and 48 pitches in the 4-1 World Series Game 5 loss to the...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays season came to an end Wednesday night following a 4 -1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 5 of the World Series. And while Tampa Bay had several opportunities to extend its season, one of the biggest questions surrounded Kevin Cash's decision to remove Drew Rasmussen after just four innings.

Rasmussen allowed one earned run across four innings, surrendering just two hits while striking out four Milwaukee batters.

However, despite throwing only 48 pitches, Cash decided to turn to his bullpen.

Following the contest, Cash explained that the decision had already been made before Rasmussen took the mound.

"We had gone into the game saying it was 60 pitches or four innings. Stuck to that. That was the easiest call in the world to take him out of the ball game," Cash said.

The Rays manager also emphasized the importance of protecting his pitchers, especially considering Rasmussen was pitching on short rest.

"We've worked very hard with all of our pitchers and pride ourselves on doing right by them. We knew this was a big ask."

Unfortunately, Tampa Bay's bullpen couldn't prevent Milwaukee from extending its lead, ultimately ending the Rays' hopes of winning their first World Series championship.

And while the decision will likely receive criticism, Cash made it clear that he appreciated Rasmussen's willingness to take the mound.

"He's a stud. That guy is a stud. His stuff was as sharp as it could have been."

However, the disappointment extended well beyond Wednesday's pitching decisions.

Cash admitted that losing the World Series was difficult, especially considering how much the players accomplished throughout the season.

"I'm crushed right now, disappointed, but it's easier to handle because of what we all meant to each other throughout the course of this season," Cash said.

Tampa Bay finished with 106 combined regular-season and postseason victories, the most in franchise history, while capturing the American League pennant.

And despite falling short of the championship, Cash emphasized the relationships developed throughout the year.

"It's as close-knit as a group as I've ever been around," Cash said.

He also credited Milwaukee's pitching for Tampa Bay's offensive struggles, describing the Brewers' bullpen as one of the best he has ever seen. In the five-game World Series, Tampa Bay's offense struggled considerably, scoring just 12 runs while batting .182 (30-for-165) with only eight extra-base hits and 40 strikeouts.

As for the future, Cash expressed excitement about the talent returning to Tampa Bay, including players who missed time because of injuries.

However, with uncertainty surrounding baseball's upcoming offseason, Cash offered one final comment when asked about what comes next.

Things look rosy once again for defending champions the New York Knicks as they produced their second straight win to move up to 2-3 for the season. New York won against the Chicago Bulls 133-127 after producing a 111-97 win over the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday.

Speaking after the game, Karl-Anthony Towns had a hilarious response to a reporter who wanted to know what he thought was the reason behind Josh Hart 's energy, per a post on X by ClutchPoints. KAT initially thought he was going to be asked a different question, but had a simple response.

"Oh, I thought you were gonna say something completely different," he said. "Sugar."

Needless to say, Josh Hart produced another high-energy display that saw him grab eight rebounds in addition to two points and three assists. Towns himself produced another commanding display, this time a double-double of 19 points and 13 rebounds along with five assists. However, for the second win running, it was Jalen Brunson who was the star of the show.

Brunson appeared to be at his dominant best for the first time this season as he finished with 38 points, seven assists and two steals in 35 minutes. Meanwhile, KAT and Landry Shamet both had injury scares in the first half.

Towns appeared to hurt his wrist after a collision with Chicago's Noa Essengue, while Shamet ended up twisting his ankle after a dunk. Regardless, Shamet was an important contributor off the bench, finishing with 14 points and five assists.

The same could be said about Jordan Clarkson, who had 18 points and three rebounds along with two steals. OG Anunoby was the second-highest scorer on the Knicks behind Brunson, producing 23 points on 7-16 shooting, also grabbing six rebounds.

New York will now travel to Philadelphia to take on the Philadelphia 76ers for the second time this season, after losing their opening-day game against LeBron James and co.

articles.title: Can Oilers’ Connor McDavid beat Wayne Gretzky’s unreal 50-point record?
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid snatched another Wayne Gretzky record on Wednesday night. He provided two assists in the Oilers’ win over the Calgary...
articles.body:
Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid snatched another Wayne Gretzky record on Wednesday night. He provided two assists in the Oilers' win over the Calgary Flames on home ice. This gives the Edmonton captain the longest season-opening assist record in NHL history.

McDavid now has 36 points through 13 games after defeating the Flames. This is an incredible run that has not been seen in the NHL in decades. "Generational" is a word oft overused. In this instance, though, it absolutely fits.

Edmonton's captain is staring down the barrel of some incredible history this season. One of those major records is actually right over the horizon. Let's take a look at whether Connor McDavid can take down Gretzky's 50-point record in 2026-27.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Connor McDavid is chasing Wayne Gretzky's 50-point record

The record in question is the speed at which a player has reached 50 points in a single season. This record belongs to Wayne Gretzky. He scored 50 points in just 18 games during the 1983-84 campaign. Gretzky ended that season with 87 goals and 205 points.

McDavid is currently on track to match this, at the very least. He has scored 2.77 points per game at this time. Across an 18-game stretch, this works out to about 49.86 points. If he maintains his current point pace, he can match this record.

It's also quite conceivable he surpasses it over the next five games. McDavid has to score 12 points in five games to beat the record. His season can be broken down into two five-game stretches. In his first five-game stretch, he scored three goals and 13 points. The second five-game stretch saw him score five goals and 18 points.

McDavid has shown the ability to put up the points he needs in this short amount of time. Whether he can become the fastest to 50 points in a single season remains to be seen. However, at his current rate, it isn't entirely out of the question this year.
